title: Sealed law, drand round 6605629: missed

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz from a law drawn by drand round 6605629, named before the round existed and sealed (SHA-256 committed and pushed) before the run

narration.transcript: a block on a spring, filmed from the side

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text or narration indicates slow motion

subjects.description: small red rectangular block hanging from the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A red block suspended from a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the centre of the frame. It starts near its lowest extended position and continues oscillating throughout the clip without being caught or stopping.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows ~0.7-0.8 s period vertical oscillation around ~100 pix with slowly shrinking amplitude, classic spring-mass. I propose undamped as baseline, linear viscous damped as textbook in-air model, and linear plus quadratic drag to capture faster-than-linear decay at high speed.

All spring variants leave almost the same wavy misses
critique.finding: The block hangs around {s0} and wobbles with quickness {omega}, slowly losing energy at {gamma} with stiffness tweak {beta}. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a clear wavy pattern in its misses.
critique.headline: Spring block wobbles with slight hardening, but pattern remains unexplained
critique.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction that makes the swing shrink in a straight-line way rather than only smooth viscous loss. The misses swing at the wobble rhythm with large size, showing the current damping gets the shrinking envelope wrong.
critique.why_it_won: It allows gentle energy loss and a tiny change of stiffness with stretch, so it follows the up-and-down wobble while plain springs or falling models drift away.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add a cubic hardening to the spring force so timing shifts with size of swing. Misses grow into larger repeating swings over time because the plain spring keeps slightly wrong time as the bounce continues.

postRevision.revision_idea: Add dry Coulomb friction that makes the swing shrink in a straight-line way rather than only smooth viscous loss. The misses swing at the wobble rhythm with large size, showing the current damping gets the shrinking envelope wrong.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a lopsided spring with viscous damping and a drive. Missed: the drive's line was in the misses, but code labelled it a sideband.
finding: The block hangs around about 110 pixel and wobbles with quickness about 9 rad/s, slowly losing energy at about 0.47 1/s with stiffness tweak about -0.001 1/(pixel² s²). It only partly captures the motion, leaving a clear wavy pattern in its misses.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6605629). The round was named in 3bc0190 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in d846c66 before the clip was rendered; the run used commit 0b852c8 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in b1902a4. Missed. The drawn law was a lopsided spring with viscous damping and a periodic drive at 13.13 rad/s. The misses of Muse Spark's best law peaked at 13.19 rad/s, 130 times the noise, but a second peak at 4.21 rad/s sat mirrored about the motion's own 8.70 rad/s with an amplitude within a factor 2, so code's spectrum labelled both a sideband pair (a swing whose amplitude or frequency changes) rather than an unexplained line, and added no drive. Muse Wonder read the same labels with its residual_spectrum tool and wrote a hardening spring; the cubic term came out within 2σ of zero, so the winner is a linear spring with viscous damping. Its two constants land within 1σ of the drawn ones, but the lopsided stiffness and the drive are missing. It misses the unseen frames by 128 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - (k2/m) x^2 - b x' + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

k2.rule: k2 A / k uniform in [0.2, 0.45], stiffer stretched (drawn 0.319)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.271)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.454)

sealed.narration: a block on a spring, filmed from the side
sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner: linear (ω), viscous γ = 0.47 ± 0.22 (2.1σ, present), cubic β = −0.0010 ± 0.0014 (0.7σ, absent); drawn: linear, quadratic (lopsided), viscous, drive. Term sets differ: no lopsided term and no drive.

spectrumAtScoring.summary: Residual spectrum of “Linearly damped spring” on the fitted frames (its misses, fitted as sinusoids one at a time, strongest first): strongest at ω = 13.19 rad/s (period 0.476 s), amplitude 130 × the noise (21.0 px in s): one of a pair mirrored about the motion's own frequency with like amplitudes, the motion's own amplitude or frequency changing over the clip (the form of the damping or the stiffness), not a drive; next at ω = 4.21 rad/s (period 1.493 s), amplitude 79.6 × the noise (12.9 px in s): one of a pair mirrored about the motion's own frequency with like amplitudes, the motion's own amplitude or frequency changing over the clip (the form of the damping or the stiffness), not a drive; next at ω = 1.25 rad/s (period 5.037 s), amplitude 56.4 × the noise (9.12 px in s): under two cycles in the fitted 4.5 s, a slow drift, not resolvable as a periodic force. The motion's own frequency is 8.70 rad/s.
